facts.text: The county’s August 17, 2026 construction update says the Simon Kenton Way entrance to the Government Center lot closes August 18 and lot access is then only via Pike Street, with work expected until spring 2027. This is a vehicle-lot instruction; confirm the pedestrian route and doorway separately.
facts.quote: The entrance from Simon Kenton Way will close on Tuesday, Aug. 18, until Spring of 2027. After that point, access to the Government Center lot will be available only via Pike Street.

facts.text: The county says the Government Center remains open during the Brent Spence project. Allow extra travel time and follow posted signs as traffic patterns change; the notice does not verify that previously forecast road reopenings occurred.
facts.quote: Residents are encouraged to allow extra travel time and follow posted signage as traffic patterns adjust during construction.

facts.text: The construction notice names the Historic Kenton County Courthouse at 5272 Madison Pike in Independence as an alternative for Sheriff, Clerk and PVA services. Confirm that the particular service you need is offered there before changing your destination.
facts.quote: Even with roadway changes, residents have convenient alternatives for many local government services at the Historic Kenton County Courthouse, located at 5272 Madison Pike in Independence. Services available there include: Kenton County Sheriff’s Office Kenton County Clerk’s Office Kenton County Property Valuation Administrator (PVA)

facts.text: The Clerk publishes Covington office hours of Monday–Friday, 7:30 a.m.–4 p.m. Its main line is 859-392-1600 and motor-vehicle line 859-392-1652. These are Clerk service details, not hours for all Government Center offices.
facts.quote: Phone Lines Service Phone Main Line 859-392-1600 Motor Vehicles 859-392-1652

facts.text: The Clerk lists closures for November 26–27, 2026 for Thanksgiving. Check its current office calendar before a trip.

facts.text: The Clerk links a 2026 General Election pictorial of polling locations. The linked guide includes Government Center exterior, entrance and interior photographs; it is election-specific preparation rather than a current construction-route walkthrough.

facts.text: The leisure pool has zero-depth entry and a maximum depth of 3.5 feet. UC lists its typical temperature as 84°F and features including a current channel, waterwall and vortex; entry equipment and transfer procedures are not specified.
facts.quote: The shallow-water Leisure Pool has a zero-depth entry with a maximum depth of 3.5 feet and is typically 84 degrees.

facts.text: The separate lap pool ranges from 4 feet to 13.5 feet deep and is typically 79°F. Lane availability changes throughout the day because it also hosts UC swimming and diving practices and meets; check the linked lane schedule.
facts.quote: The Lap Pool is 50 meters by 23 meters (25 yards) and is typically 79 degrees. The Lap Pool features two 1-meter diving boards and a 3-meter diving board. Depth varies from 4 feet to 13.5 feet. Open recreation swim lanes are available for members throughout the day. The pool also plays host to our UC Swim and Dive teams for practices and meets. Lane availability changes throughout the day

facts.text: Campus Green and Woodside are the garages UC identifies as closest to the CRC. Parking is not automatically included with membership; the source does not describe a continuous garage-to-door route.
facts.quote: Campus Green and Woodside garages are the closest to the CRC.

facts.text: Members must normally enter and exit through the main lobby. The policy allows other exits in an emergency; confirm the doorway and any assistance needed before visiting.
facts.quote: Except in the case of an emergency, members must enter and exit the Campus Recreation Center through the main lobby.

facts.text: Community memberships are offered to Greater Cincinnati residents aged 18 or older and include pools, courts and fitness facilities. UC student status is not required for this membership.
facts.quote: Our doors are open to the greater Cincinnati community through Campus Rec memberships. With a membership, you’ll have access to state-of-the-art fitness equipment, group fitness classes, pools, courts, and more, all in a welcoming, energetic environment. Whether you’re looking to get stronger, stay active, or meet new people, Campus Rec is a great place to move and connect. Individuals eligible for this membership must be 18 years of age or older.

facts.text: Bring a valid physical photo ID to the Member Services Desk. The entry policy does not accept pictures or photocopies of an ID.
facts.quote: All individuals must present a valid, physical photo ID (no pictures or photocopies) at the Member Services Desk to obtain access to the facility.

facts.text: UC’s first-visit guide places cardio/weights, racquetball, group fitness, track and cycling upstairs, and climbing, gym courts, pools and locker rooms downstairs. The guide does not describe the elevator route between these areas.
facts.quote: Go upstairs for cardio and weight equipment, racquetball courts, group fitness classes, track, and cycle studio. Go downstairs for climbing wall, gym courts, pools, and locker rooms.

facts.text: The first-visit guide identifies 5–9 p.m. as the busiest period and suggests early morning, lunchtime or weekends for more space. This is general crowd guidance, not a designated quiet session.
facts.quote: Campus Rec gets busiest from 5–9 p.m. If you like plenty of space to do your thing, hit up an early morning workout, swing by at lunch, or check us out on the weekends.

facts.text: The posted pool cleaning closures are Monday 8 a.m.–noon for the leisure pool and Wednesday 8 a.m.–noon for the lap pool. Check the pool and alternate-hours pages before travelling.
facts.quote: Leisure Pool is closed for cleaning every Monday 8 a.m. - 12 p.m.

facts.text: UC says all pools close 30 minutes before the rest of the CRC. Holiday and break hours may differ from the posted fall schedule.
facts.quote: All pools close 30 minutes before the rest of the Campus Recreation Center.

facts.text: The locker-room rules provide family changing rooms for members with small children of the opposite sex. They do not describe adult assisted-changing facilities, equipment or dimensions.
facts.quote: Family changing rooms are available for members with small children of the opposite sex.

facts.text: UC’s single-occupancy restroom list includes CRC rooms 0222A–D, 0M300B/C, 1223/1224, 1352/1353, 2100A/B and 2355. The list also marks rooms 3356, 4356, 5356 and 6356 as available only to UC students. It does not establish transfer space or adult changing equipment.

Day-use lockers are free and first-come. CRC locker rooms and gym-court lockers use built-in combination locks; fitness-floor and climbing-wall day lockers use personal locks. Remove locks and belongings by closing; ask Member Services about reach and assistance.
facts.quote: There is no fee for day-use lockers; they can be utilized on a first-come, first-served basis. Visit the Member Services Desk for locker rental and towel service. Availability When using a locker at the Campus Recreation Center , a member will either use the built-in combination lock (in locker rooms and at gym courts) or use a personal lock (fitness floor and climbing wall) depending on locker type.

facts.text: Campus Rec member parking cards must be scanned on entry and exit; do not pull a ticket. Each card allows three hours once per day while using Campus Rec, with additional charges after three hours. At a gate problem, press HELP on the card reader.
facts.quote: Parking cards with barcodes are used for Campus Recreation member parking. You must scan the card in to be able to later scan out (do not pull a ticket on entry). Hold card under red barcode reader (see photo at the top of this page) to enter/exit the garage. Each card entitles the designated permit holder to 3 hours of parking once per day while using Campus Rec facilities. Additional fees will automatically begin after 3 hours and will be charged at exit.

facts.text: For CRC visit planning, call Member Services at 513-556-0604. The Campus Rec contact page also lists campusrec@uc.edu for questions.
facts.quote: Send us an email at campusrec@uc.edu .

facts.text: The first-visit guide says fitness staff can give a personal tour of the fitness floor and show how to use and adjust equipment; stop at the Fitness Desk to ask.
facts.quote: Fitness Staff will give you a personal tour of the fitness floor and show you how to use and adjust the equipment. Just stop by the Fitness Desk anytime!

facts.text: CRC’s facility register lists Dunham’s Otto Armleder Regional Aquatic Center as a shallow pool with zero-depth entry, a slide and a sprayground. It does not give slopes, transfer procedures or water-wheelchair details.
facts.quote: Dunham: Otto Armleder Regional Aquatic Center Dunham 4356 Dunham Lane Cincinnati, Ohio 45238 Shallow, Zero Depth Entry, Slide, Sprayground

facts.text: The published 2026 pool table gives Dunham an August 8 season closing date. This is a summer schedule, not confirmation of November swimming or next year’s dates.
facts.quote: Dunham Otto Armleder members only swim open swim members only entry* 6/6 8/8

facts.text: In its summer 2026 guidance, CRC restricts new entry after 4:30 p.m. Friday–Sunday to Dunham pool members; non-member guests already inside may stay and swim. Confirm the next season’s rules before relying on this policy.
facts.quote: Due to capacity considerations, Dunham Otto Armleder Pool restricts entry from 4:30pm to closing for members only. Other guests are welcome to stay and swim but cannot enter after 4:30pm Friday - Sunday.

facts.text: The recreation-center page lists Monday–Friday hours of 9 a.m.–8 p.m. and weekends as available for rentals. Call 513-251-5862 for the current program, membership or rental arrangements; these are not pool opening hours.
facts.quote: Monday 9:00 AM – 8:00 PM Tuesday 9:00 AM – 8:00 PM Wednesday 9:00 AM – 8:00 PM Thursday 9:00 AM – 8:00 PM Friday 9:00 AM – 8:00 PM Saturday Available for rentals Sunday Available for rentals

facts.text: CRC asks people needing additional program assistance to request an Accommodation and Assessment Form at registration at the recreation center. This systemwide process does not guarantee a particular Dunham arrangement.
facts.quote: If you feel an accommodation would be beneficial or necessary, please request an Accommodation and Assessment Form at the time of registration at the recreation center. This document is used to formally request additional assistance you may require.

facts.text: CRC’s Inclusion Team lists Boardmaker communication tools, adaptive equipment, increased supervision and behavior supports among possible accommodation types. Confirm the support for the particular Dunham program; this is not a local equipment inventory.
facts.quote: Types of Accommodations Changes in Rules and/or Policies Assistance with ADLs (activities of daily living) Architectural Changes Adaptive Equipment Increased Supervision Behavior Supports Specialized Training for Staff Boardmaker Tools for Communication

facts.text: CRC says some programs, fitness use and pool use carry separate fees. A center membership alone does not establish admission to every Dunham activity.
facts.quote: Please Note: Separate fees apply for certain programs, fitness access, and pool access.
Accessible tickets can be purchased online via www.livenation.com but are not required to use our accessible seating section.

Unfortunately, given the age of our building, we do not have an elevator to our upstairs level. We do offer ADA seats on the Mezzanine and there is a wheelchair elevator to take guests from the Mezzanine to the main floor.

Accessible drop off is located at Corey and Short Vine or in front of the crosswalk in front of our venue. Metered parking is available on the street (free on Sunday, holidays, and weekdays after 6pm). Arrival & Accessible Entrances Our Great Bands Entrance is fully accessible.
Please note Bogart's does not own or operate parking but there are several garages and street parking within one to two blocks of the venue.
Please see a member of the guest services team upon your arrival. They will provide you with an Assisted Listening Device in exchange for an ID that will be securely held in the box office.

Bogart's offers sign language interpretation upon request only. Requests for interpreters must be received at least two weeks before the event date. Please make your request by calling 513.872.8801 or emailing BogartsBoxOffice@livenation.com and include how many in your party need interpretation and the ticket type you have. Interpretation requests are subject to the availability of an interpreter.
Most events only offer General Admission standing and seating, which are first-come, first-serve. Please refer to the event page for seating options by event.
For more questions, or information not mentioned below, don't hesitate to get in touch with us at 513.872.8801 or BogartsBoxOffice@livenation.com
Our accessible bathroom is located on our Mezzanine.
We cannot store any type of medication.
We will do our best to store mobility devices for guests as needed.

facts.text: Bogart’s asks visitors bringing prescribed medication to bring only what is needed for the event in its original labelled container, with a name verifiable by photo ID. It may request documentation if the container is not labelled. Over-the-counter medication must be in its original packaging; medication storage is unavailable.
facts.quote: If you need to enter with prescribed medication to be taken during the event, we require that all medication be in its original container with a name that is verifiable with a photo ID. If you do not have a container with a name on it, we may request documentation that allows us to confirm the need for this medication as you enter the venue. Please only bring what is required for the duration of the event. We cannot store any type of medication. Over-the-counter medication must be in its original packaging.

facts.text: The venue has a limited snack menu. Ask Food & Beverage staff about dietary needs; Bogart’s says it will make reasonable efforts but cannot guarantee meeting every request.
facts.quote: Our venue has a limited snack menu during events. You may request to speak with a member of our Food & Beverage team with specific questions or concerns. While we will make reasonable efforts to accommodate dietary requests, we cannot guarantee that they will be able to meet all requests.

facts.text: Bogart’s is cashless and lists a fee-free cash-to-card kiosk on site. The page does not specify the kiosk’s location, controls or reach.
facts.quote: Bogart's is cashless and offers a fee free cash-to-card kiosk on site.

facts.text: The Clerk offers certified marriage-license copies by online request or written mail request. It asks you first to check that the license was issued in Kenton County. These are alternatives to an office visit, with separate service and postage costs listed on the source page.
facts.quote: Marriage license : Before requesting a marriage license, verify that the license was issued in Kenton County. Search using this free link: MARRIAGE RECORD INDEX Request certified copies online at: Marriage Requests .
